page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.14xlarge is a dedicated server instance from the Big data family, configured to handle massive data storage and batch processing requirements. Operating on the KVM hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture, the machine is driven by 56 dedicated vCPUs from the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor family running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. It includes 224.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators, focusing hardware resources entirely on general compute, throughput, and capacity.

Storage density forms the primary technical distinction of the ecs.d1ne.14xlarge. The instance bundles 165,356 GB of local HDD storage, offering substantial bulk storage directly attached to the host. Networking capabilities are matched with a 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, facilitating sustained transfers between nodes in multi-server architectures. While the spinning disk configuration yields high sequential throughput and deep volume, it trades off the high random IOPS and ultra-low latency characteristic of NVMe SSD alternatives.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high storage-per-core economics, avoiding the cost premium of solid-state storage arrays while retaining high aggregate compute throughput across 56 cores. This hardware profile is well suited for distributed big data processing, Apache Hadoop or Spark worker clusters, log aggregation systems, data lakes, and ETL pipelines that process massive sequential datasets over distributed storage architectures.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.14xlarge is a high-capacity big data instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors, it delivers 56 vCPUs paired with 224.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The defining characteristic of this configuration is its integrated dense storage profile, supplying 165,356 GB of local HDD capacity along with a 35 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Containing no hardware accelerators, this server prioritizes deep sequential storage volume and network capacity over GPU compute. The combination of extensive local disk arrays and robust networking makes the instance cost-effective for sequential data pipelines and massive data footprints. Best-fit workloads include distributed file systems, Apache Hadoop or Spark infrastructure, log analytics, and large-scale batch ETL processing.
